extras.name: BASELINE: largest context window that stays on the RTX 5090, per Ollama model (E5 method)
extras.note: For each model, the largest num_ctx whose confirm (a prompt filling about 90% of the window, one generated token) stays fully on the card, under the ceiling, with no spill into shared (system) memory. The search loads windows on a 2,048-token grid from the trained cap down, then confirms upward from the floor. A slope predictor built from two measured loads skips windows forecast over the ceiling. The shared-memory gate applies only near the ceiling (peak at least 28,452 MiB), because Windows counts the pinned host buffers each load reserves (CUDA_Host) as shared GPU memory: about 352 MiB for qwen3:8b and 1,128 MiB for gemma4:31b. Ollama 0.35.1, NVIDIA driver 617.42, CUDA 13.4, f16 KV cache with flash attention, Q4_K_M weights, idle card, 30,500 MiB ceiling. Measured by interlock's E5 (fill-card) on 2026-10-13; trimmed records in rnd's experiments/e5, receipts in interlock's receipts/.

extras.name: BASELINE: the RTX 5090 keeps its decode speed beside the Intel NPU or iGPU (E4b)
extras.note: Interlock's E4b ran alone, paired, alone triplets and scored each as a log-ratio: Hodges-Lehmann estimate, exact Wilcoxon 90% interval, pre-registered as free when the interval lies inside +/-10%. All four pairs are free. The 5090's decode rate changed -0.83% [-1.20, -0.46] beside the NPU and +0.57% [+0.24, +1.38] beside the iGPU. With a 5090 companion decoding steadily, NPU latency changed -0.61% [-1.31, +0.06] and iGPU latency +2.48% [-0.99, +4.82]. So a router can treat the 5090 and the Intel devices as independent lanes. Clock tolerance and steady band 22.5 MHz; NVML probe at 0.206 s; peak VRAM about 12.6 GB. Measured 2026-10-12 (receipts e4b-block-2 and e4b-block-3).

research.notes: Ollama behaviour measured on the rig, via rnd.

extras.name: RECIPE: Ollama - num_predict 0, null or missing means no completion limit
extras.note: On Ollama 0.35.1, a generate request with num_predict 0 (or null, or missing) does not mean count the prompt only: the model generates until end of turn or a full context. Measured on the RTX 5090: num_predict 0 gave no reply within 90 s, while num_predict 1 returned prompt_eval_count 221 in 3.0 s. Missing, null and 0 each generated 144 tokens on qwen3:8b against 1 for num_predict 1, and a small num_ctx (64) did not bound it. To count a prompt's tokens, ask for one token and read prompt_eval_count. Refuse a num_predict that is 0, null, missing or not a positive integer before the request is sent. A test fake that accepts 0 hides this.

extras.name: RECIPE: counting a long prompt's tokens through Ollama - estimate, then bisect the tail
extras.note: Each token count is a model call that re-reads the whole prompt. Growing a prompt one seed sentence per count took thousands of counts for a 118k-token target and over 30 minutes, though Ollama prefilled 122k tokens in 19.6 s on the RTX 5090. Estimate the repeats from the seed's own count, check one repeat below, then bisect only the remaining tail: 25 counts or fewer at 118k, with the same result. Keep a cold re-count of the final prefix, because a prompt cache can undercount. Test a search against a live model for how many calls it makes, not only for its answer.

research.notes: CUDA stack and rented-host checks, via rnd.

extras.name: BASELINE: the studio rig's CUDA stack (RTX 5090, sm_120)
extras.note: Measured 2026-10-07: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, compute capability 12.0 (consumer Blackwell, sm_120), driver 617.14 (617.42 by 2026-10-13), nvcc 13.4.59. On 617.x, nvidia-smi prints 'CUDA UMD Version: 13.4' instead of the older 'CUDA Version:', so a parser must accept both forms. ComfyUI's embedded torch 2.12.0+cu130 includes sm_120. A separate Python 3.12 environment with torch 2.14.1+cu130 reaches about 223 TFLOPS on an 8192x8192 fp16 matmul. The system's default Python carries a CPU-only torch build. Re-measure after a driver or toolkit upgrade.

extras.name: RECIPE: check a rented GPU host's driver and download speed before paying
extras.note: On rented RunPod hosts two properties vary per host, not per GPU type: the driver, and /workspace and Hugging Face download speed. torch 2.13.0+cu130 (pulled by vllm 0.31.0) needs an R580+ driver: it failed with 'driver too old' on an A100 host on 570.195.03 and worked on one on 580.126.16. Within one data centre, /workspace writes ranged from 32 MB/s to 238-540 MB/s an hour apart, and one Hugging Face stream from 1.9 to 74 MB/s. A container disk (180 GB, with HF_HOME on it) wrote at about 1.3 GB/s. In the first 30 seconds, read the driver (accepting both nvidia-smi print forms; refuse a CUDA 13 wheel below R580) and measure a /workspace write and one HF stream. Abort and re-rent a slow host, and gate on time-to-ready as well.
